🇮🇱🇮🇷🇺🇸 Israel may change prime ministers before the next Iran strike: Eisenkot just vowed to force a vote to replace Netanyahu

Danny Citrinowicz used to run the Iran desk for Israeli military intelligence, and right now he’s worried about his own prime minister.

Netanyahu is a caretaker who can’t build a coalition, and Danny lays out why that makes war tempting.

A new fight with Iran could push his rivals into a unity government under him, and after January 3 a Democratic Congress makes it much harder for Trump to say yes.

Danny on why the pressure on Washington is peaking this month:

“So this is the golden moment.”

Gadi Eisenkot has until December 6 to take the job, and Danny expects him to drop the push because his biggest problems are at home.

Iran still gets a vote, though, with tankers lined up to test the blockade and a habit of choosing escalation every time it’s cornered.

@citrinowicz @WeTheBrandon

🇺🇸🇺🇦🇷🇺 Kushner reportedly offered Ukraine NATO membership for giving up Donbas... Kyiv won’t hand over land and Moscow won’t accept NATO

A peace plan needs at least one side to want it, and this one is 0 for 2 so far with Germany against it as well.

Dimitri Lascaris, a Canadian lawyer and journalist who has reported from Crimea, can’t see why Russia would drop a red line it has held since the 1990s while it’s gaining ground.

He’s more worried about what followed this week’s three strikes on the Crimean Bridge, because Putin’s answer to every attack has been the same:

“They hit Ukraine five times as hard. Has that stopped Ukraine from attacking their infrastructure? No.”

Dimitri expects Moscow to eventually hit a NATO target to make the attacks stop, possibly within a year, and he’s clear he doesn’t want that.

So who talks both sides down before the next bridge, when the only offer on the table is one they’ve each already refused?

@dimitrilascaris @WeTheBrandon
